lines.text: The phrase first water began with diamonds.
In the gem trade, water meant a stone's clearness.
A perfect diamond was the clearest drop of water.
There were three ranks, from first water down to third.
Some think it came from Arabic, where water also means luster.
Shakespeare wrote of diamonds of a most praised water around 1607.

lines.text: It even described crooks, like a swindler of the first water.
Jewelers once called the most colorless diamonds river or first water.

post.caption: The phrase first water began with diamonds. In the gem trade, water meant a stone's clearness, and a perfect diamond was the clearest drop of water. There were three ranks, from first water down to third. Some think it came from Arabic, where water also means luster. Shakespeare wrote of diamonds of a most praised water around 1607. By about 1800 people used it for anything the very best, and it even described crooks, like a swindler of the first water. Jewelers once called the most colorless diamonds river or first water. GIA's D to Z color scale arrived in 1953.
